title: o-sfu Performance Signals
description: Performance evidence at matched workload: RTT tails and bucket shares, reported loss, throughput, fanout, saturation, recovery and signaling delay. Missing instrumentation is explicit.

options.content:
Compare the same codec, bitrate, topology and fanout. All rates and distributions use a **rolling 5-minute window**. Add annotations for load steps and revisions. Cards show the end of the selected range.

**RTT is a histogram estimate** with a 50 ms first bucket. Jitter p95 and SFU forwarding delay are not exported. Use the observation counts and measurement limits below when comparing runs.

panels.title: Metrics evidence
panels.description: A successful SFU scrape no older than 60 seconds is required for the selected range endpoint. No data remains unavailable rather than becoming zero.

panels.title: Peer RTT p95
panels.description: Estimated p95 of sampled TWCC peer RTT. Observation-weighted, not packet- or user-weighted. The 50 ms first bucket cannot resolve sub-50 ms tails. Values above the 5 s finite ceiling need the overflow share below.

panels.title: Egress loss
panels.description: Mean of available reported egress loss observations, mixing peer TWCC and media RTCP reports. Not a ratio of total lost packets to total sent packets. Zero observations remain unavailable.

panels.title: Egress payload
panels.description: RTP payload accepted into local RTC senders per second. Excludes transport headers and does not confirm receiver delivery.

panels.title: Peer RTT estimates
panels.description: TWCC peer RTT distributions, kept separate from stream RTCP RTT. Histogram interpolation estimates p50/p95/p99. Buckets are 50, 100, 250 and 500 ms, then 1, 2 and 5 s. These measure a round trip, not SFU forwarding residence time.

panels.title: Stream RTT p95 estimates
panels.description: Separate ingress RTCP XR DLRR and egress receiver-report RTT observations. Each family has its own sample count and can be absent independently. These are not ICE/STUN RTT or one-way delay.

panels.title: Reported loss means
panels.description: Observation-weighted loss fractions. Peer TWCC and media RTCP reports share each direction counter. The server clamps finite reports to 0..1. These means are not packet-weighted loss or loss percentiles.

panels.title: Peer RTT bucket shares
panels.description: Cumulative shares at actual exporter boundaries, plus the share above the largest finite bucket. The first three shares overlap and must not be added. These boundaries are measurement resolution, not health thresholds. A p95/p99 in the overflow bucket reports the 5 s ceiling rather than the actual larger latency.

targets.expr: ((sum by (instance) (rate(osfu_media_quality_rtt_seconds_count{instance=~"$instance",sample="peer"}[5m])) - sum by (instance) (rate(osfu_media_quality_rtt_seconds_bucket{instance=~"$instance",sample="peer",le="5"}[5m]))) / (sum by (instance) (rate(osfu_media_quality_rtt_seconds_count{instance=~"$instance",sample="peer"}[5m])) > 0)) and on (instance) (osfu:metrics_available{instance=~"$instance"} == 1)

panels.title: RTT observations / 5m
panels.description: Field-specific observed RTT counts, separately for peer, media_ingress and media_egress. Quality sampling defaults to five seconds and may be disabled. Prometheus increase can extrapolate fractional counts.

panels.title: Loss observations / 5m
panels.description: Only observations carrying the corresponding loss value count. A generic media-quality event does not establish loss availability.

panels.title: RTP packet rate
panels.description: RTP ingress and local egress packet rates. Packet rate measures work that bitrate alone can hide. Egress counts local sender acceptance.

panels.title: RTP payload throughput
panels.description: Payload bits per second, excluding UDP/IP/DTLS/SRTP headers. This is not network-interface wire bandwidth.

panels.title: Rooms and users
panels.description: Current workload population over the selected time range. Equal user counts can produce different SFU work depending on publications and subscriptions.

panels.title: Publications and subscriptions
panels.description: Current committed or pending media entries. They are not distinct publishers/subscribers or proof of flowing media.

panels.title: RTP egress by worker
panels.description: Local egress packet rate per bounded worker ID. Compare worker distribution at matched room placement and fanout.

panels.title: Local forwarding fanout
panels.description: Local RTC forwarding operations per ingress RTP packet. Values above one are normal fanout. Zero ingress leaves the ratio unavailable. This is not a delivery-success or packet-loss ratio.

panels.title: Relay mailbox mean depth
panels.description: Mailbox depth sampled on relay enqueue attempts. This is traffic-weighted mean occupancy, not a time-weighted queue length or queue-wait delay.

panels.title: Worker egress concentration
panels.description: Largest worker payload egress divided by the mean among exported workers. One means equal rates. Room locality may legitimately concentrate traffic. Idle traffic stays unavailable.

targets.expr: (max by (instance) (sum by (instance, media_worker_id) (rate(osfu_worker_rtp_payload_bytes_total{instance=~"$instance",direction="egress"}[5m]))) / (avg by (instance) (sum by (instance, media_worker_id) (rate(osfu_worker_rtp_payload_bytes_total{instance=~"$instance",direction="egress"}[5m]))) > 0)) and on (instance) (osfu:metrics_available{instance=~"$instance"} == 1)

panels.title: Relay and control backpressure
panels.description: Distinct backpressure events per second. A drain cap hit means packets remain for a later turn. These counters are not independent lost-packet totals and must not be summed into a loss percentage.

panels.title: Transport protection events
panels.description: Server protection boundaries. Output budget exhaustion can close a session. RTCP datagram rejections and session closures have different denominators from media packet loss.

panels.title: WebSocket queue depth
panels.description: Current queued outbound room messages. Inspect shutdown rate and control-plane latency when depth grows. This is not media queue delay.

panels.title: Generic NACK demand
panels.description: NACK feedback events sent to publishers or received from subscribers. One feedback event can request multiple packets. These rates do not measure packet-loss fraction.

panels.title: Publisher RTX received
panels.description: Authenticated publisher repair packets accepted after de-RTX. No claim of successful subscriber recovery is made.

panels.title: Keyframe recovery events
panels.description: Forwarded/coalesced requests, retries and decoder-refresh clears. Observe recovery work without treating event ratios as per-request success.

panels.title: WebSocket readiness delay estimates
panels.description: Time from WebSocket upgrade through readiness or rejection, including auth waiting. Histograms include failures. This is neither ICE/DTLS setup time nor time to first media. Finite buckets start at 10 ms and end at 5 s, so the estimates have limited resolution.

targets.expr: (histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (instance, le) (rate(osfu_ws_handshake_duration_seconds_bucket{instance=~"$instance"}[5m]))) and on (instance) (sum by (instance) (increase(osfu_ws_handshake_duration_seconds_count{instance=~"$instance"}[5m])) > 0)) and on (instance) (osfu:metrics_available{instance=~"$instance"} == 1)

(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (instance, le) (rate(osfu_ws_handshake_duration_seconds_bucket{instance=~"$instance"}[5m]))) and on (instance) (sum by (instance) (increase(osfu_ws_handshake_duration_seconds_count{instance=~"$instance"}[5m])) > 0)) and on (instance) (osfu:metrics_available{instance=~"$instance"} == 1)

(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (instance, le) (rate(osfu_ws_handshake_duration_seconds_bucket{instance=~"$instance"}[5m]))) and on (instance) (sum by (instance) (increase(osfu_ws_handshake_duration_seconds_count{instance=~"$instance"}[5m])) > 0)) and on (instance) (osfu:metrics_available{instance=~"$instance"} == 1)

panels.title: Authentication and initialization p95
panels.description: Auth covers first auth wait through token validation. Initialization starts after room admission. Failures may contribute to both duration families. Keep stage counts alongside the estimates.

targets.expr: (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (instance, le) (rate(osfu_ws_auth_duration_seconds_bucket{instance=~"$instance"}[5m]))) and on (instance) (sum by (instance) (increase(osfu_ws_auth_duration_seconds_count{instance=~"$instance"}[5m])) > 0)) and on (instance) (osfu:metrics_available{instance=~"$instance"} == 1)

(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (instance, le) (rate(osfu_ws_user_initialize_duration_seconds_bucket{instance=~"$instance"}[5m]))) and on (instance) (sum by (instance) (increase(osfu_ws_user_initialize_duration_seconds_count{instance=~"$instance"}[5m])) > 0)) and on (instance) (osfu:metrics_available{instance=~"$instance"} == 1)

panels.title: Setup duration observations / 5m
panels.description: Counts for the exact duration histogram families above. Sparse or absent samples cannot establish a latency regression.

panels.title: Rejected or slow-consumer connections
panels.description: Independent connection-event rates that qualify setup latency and queue pressure. They are not matched-session failure probabilities.

panels.title: 5. Current worker service delay: configured diagnostics server

options.content:
These snapshots always query the **configured Infinity diagnostics server**, independently of the SFU selector and historical time range.

Delay is sustained heartbeat service lateness across 100 ms periods. It suppresses isolated spikes and is not packet forwarding latency. Missing heartbeats stay unavailable. Startup grace may report zero.

panels.description: Current worker count, missing heartbeat count and the largest reported delay and mailbox occupancy. Empty diagnostics results stay unavailable.

targets.root_selector: if length == 0 then [] else [{workers: length, missingHeartbeats: ([.[] | select(.pressure.packetLoopDelayMs == null)] | length), worstDelayMs: ([.[].pressure.packetLoopDelayMs | select(type == "number")] | max), maximumQueuePct: ([.[].pressure.workerPressureScore | select(type == "number")] | max)}] end

panels.title: Current worker delay and occupancy

panels.description: Current diagnostics only. Missing heartbeat is distinct from zero delay, including startup grace. Rows are ordered by missing heartbeat, delay then maximum command/relay queue occupancy. No historical worker pressure is exported.

targets.root_selector: map(. + {heartbeat: (if .pressure.packetLoopDelayMs == null then "Missing" else "Reported" end)}) | sort_by((if .pressure.packetLoopDelayMs == null then 0 else 1 end), -(.pressure.packetLoopDelayMs // 0), -(.pressure.workerPressureScore // 0), .mediaWorkerId)

panels.title: Current workers needing attention

options.content:
| Signal | Current limit |
| --- | --- |
| Jitter p95 in ms | Only a sum and count in mixed RTP clock units. Needs clock-normalized per-stream observations and histogram buckets. |
| SFU forwarding delay | No ingress-to-egress residence-time histogram. RTT, WebSocket delay and heartbeat delay measure different boundaries. |
| Historical worker delay p95 | Worker diagnostics are current snapshots and suppress isolated heartbeat spikes. No historical histogram is exported. |
| SFU CPU / memory efficiency | No process CPU/RSS export or verified mapping from the chosen SFU to a host/container exporter. Use the controlled load-test resource report. |
| Receiver delivery and playout | Sender acceptance is not receiver delivery. Browser jitter-buffer delay, freezes and decoding need receiver instrumentation. |
